identity.title: Rash, fever, arthralgia after new drug (AIN triad)

technique.how: Take a dated medication history for the preceding weeks to months (antibiotics, PPIs, NSAIDs, allopurinol, immune checkpoint inhibitors) and ask about fever, new rash, joint pains, and flank pain since starting; inspect the skin. Correlate the time course with the onset of creatinine rise.
technique.prerequisites: Complete drug list including over-the-counter and recently stopped agents.

interpretation.positive_finding: Fever, rash, or arthralgia emerging after a new drug in a patient with unexplained AKI (often with sterile pyuria) supports drug-induced AIN and should prompt stopping the drug and nephrology input.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of the triad is the rule: in biopsy series each feature is present in fewer than half of cases and the full triad in roughly 10%, so absence does not lower the probability of AIN meaningfully.
interpretation.pitfalls: PPI- and NSAID-induced AIN are typically oligosymptomatic with long latency; fever and rash after a new drug also occur with drug fever, DRESS, and infection without AIN. Definitive diagnosis requires kidney biopsy.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: stop the suspect drug, check urinalysis for pyuria/WBC casts and consider biopsy/steroids early; negative should not remove AIN from the differential of unexplained AKI on a new drug.

estimates.population: 60 adults with biopsy-proven AIN (92% drug-related) from 2598 native renal biopsies over 12 years, single center; retrospective
estimates.quote: The presenting symptoms included oliguria (51%), arthralgia (45%), fever (30%), rash (21%) and loin pain (21%).
estimates.target_condition: Biopsy-proven acute interstitial nephritis - arthralgia present (frequency among cases = sensitivity)

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of fever/rash/arthralgia to exclude AIN, especially with PPIs or NSAIDs; do not attribute fever plus AKI to AIN without considering sepsis.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rapidly rising creatinine, oliguria, or hyperkalemia on a suspect drug needs same-day nephrology review; biopsy decisions are time-sensitive because delayed drug withdrawal worsens recovery.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: History items; no reliability data found.

extraction_notes: No case-control or cohort study reporting specificity or LRs of the triad for AIN among patients with AKI was found; only case-series frequencies (sensitivity without specificity) exist, hence partially_quantified. The Zajjari triad includes eosinophilia (a lab), so it is entered as COMPOSITE and is not the pure history triad. Muriithi 2015 AJKD series (PMID 24927897; 133 biopsy-proven AIN, 70% drug-induced, PPIs 'less symptomatic') has no triad percentages in its abstract and the full text is not open access. The anchor narrative review (Perazella & Markowitz, PMID 20517290) is cited as consensus-level context only; its abstract carries no triad number.
